hypothesis: Fishing dependence has a positive residual association with jurisdictional hierarchy across Ethnographic Atlas societies after measured subsistence, ecological, geographic, and shared-history controls; settlement and population scale explain a material portion of any residual.

controls.description: Permute fishing dependence within D-PLACE macroregions to estimate a geography-preserving null distribution.
Replace fishing with hunting or gathering in matched adjusted models to test whether the result is distinctive to aquatic subsistence.
Include logged distance to coast so fishing dependence is not merely a coastline indicator.
Resample Glottolog language families and 20-degree geographic cells to expose cultural and spatial dependence.

gates.criterion: Record exact source commits, input hashes, join counts, and deterministic run command.
Registered supports and finite matrices pass, all outcome levels remain, and adjusted M1 has at least 600 complete societies.
M1 fishing coefficient is positive, the language-family block 95% interval excludes zero, and the within-region permutation p-value is at most 0.05.
EC_G2 is evaluated in the model that includes logged distance to coast.
The standardized M1 fishing coefficient exceeds matched hunting and gathering substitute coefficients.
Potential mediators improve AIC and attenuate the absolute fishing coefficient by at least 25 percent without sign reversal.
M1 fishing remains positive outside Europe, after excluding the three largest language families, and in at least six leave-one-region-out refits.
All binary-cutpoint fishing coefficients share the ordinal sign and stay within three pooled standard errors.
